name: com.cruiseregister.mcp/cruise-register
title: Cruise Register
description: Cruise prices for your party, deals, itineraries, ports, shore excursions and price alerts.

tools.name: find
tools.description: Resolve a name to the ids the other tools take: a ship ("Icon of the Seas"), a port ("Cozumel"), a cruise line ("Carnival") or a destination ("Alaska"). Call it first when the user names a place, ship or line. Returns up to 10 matches, best first.

text.description: The name as the user wrote it

tools.name: search_sailings
tools.description: Find priced cruises by destination, departure port, line, ship, dates, length, party and cabin. Returns up to 10 sailings with the all-in total for the party (fare, taxes, required charges and gratuities, as our sailing pages show it) and a link to each sailing page. On a departure from Australia, New Zealand or the UK, local_price is the line's own fare in that currency; when local_price.leads is true, quote its all_in_for_two first, then the US$ total. book_url is our booking link: link that, never a booking site by name. Use find first to turn names into ids. Quote prices only from the returned rows.

destination.description: A cruise region the sailing visits

calls_at.description: A port id (from find) the sailing calls at

line.description: Cruise line id (from find), e.g. carnival-cruise-line

party.description: Who travels: 2A two adults (default), 1A one adult, 2A2C two adults and two children

cabin.description: Cabin class; any = the cheapest cabin

max_total_usd.description: Highest all-in total for the whole party

sort.description: Order: price (Lowest price: the all-in price for two (the total the row shows)); price_high (Highest price: the all-in price for two, highest first); night (Lowest per night: the all-in price for two divided by the nights); saving (Biggest saving: furthest below the ship's usual price for similar dates); date (Soonest: the departure date); short (Shortest: the number of nights); long (Longest: the number of nights); ship (Best-rated ship: the ship's passenger score out of 5); ports (Best-rated ports: the average passenger score of the itinerary's scored ports). per_night is the same as night. saving, ship and ports order the 200 cheapest matches; sailings without the figure come last.

tools.name: get_sailing
tools.description: One sailing by id (from search_sailings): the day-by-day itinerary (port, arrival and departure times, docked or by tender, sea days) and the all-in price for the party in each cabin class. Prices only from the returned rows. When the line gives the ports without their order, itinerary is empty and ports_unordered lists them A to Z (order_confirmed false): never state an order, days or sea days then. local_prices: the line's own fares in the departure market's currency (AU, NZ, GB departures, two adults); quote all_in_for_two first when leads is true. book_url is our booking link: link that, never a booking site by name.

party.description: Who travels: 2A two adults (default), 1A one adult, 2A2C two adults and two children

tools.name: get_port
tools.description: A port from our own data: what passengers say (score, liked and watch-out points, from summarised reviews), how often ships dock or tender, typical time ashore, which lines call, whether cruises leave from it, and the climate for a month (monthly normals, not a forecast). ship_visits counts every call; with_published_hours only those with times, the same calls port_excursions' morning and afternoon call types add up to. Use port_day for one date.

port_id.description: Port id from find, e.g. un:MXCZM

tools.name: port_day
tools.description: Which cruise ships are scheduled in a port on a date, with their hours, how passengers get ashore, and about how many passengers that is at full ships, plus quiet/typical/busy against the port's own usual day. From the lines' itineraries: scheduled, not tracked.

port_id.description: Port id from find, e.g. un:MXCZM

tools.name: get_ship
tools.description: A ship by id (from find): size, age, refit, passenger capacity, what passengers say (score out of 5, liked and watch-out points, from summarised reviews), where it is scheduled today (not live tracking), and its next 10 sailings with the lowest all-in price for two.

ship_id.description: Ship id from find, e.g. icon-of-the-seas-2024

tools.name: port_excursions
tools.description: Shore excursions at a cruise port as figures across tours: how many, how many fit a ship's time ashore (for a date, or a usual morning or afternoon call), typical length and price per person (middle half), the review-weighted average rating, and the categories, plus how many tours fit one call (a ship on a date, the first call that date, or a usual morning or afternoon call; default: the port's most common) with see_tours_url, our page listing them. Figures across tours only: no single tour, price or booking link; send the user to see_tours_url for the tours themselves.

date.description: A call date: the ships in port that day and what fits each

hours_ashore.description: Time ashore, when the user knows it rather than a date

ship_id.description: With date: fit the tours to this ship's call (id from find or get_sailing)

call_type.description: Fit the tours to a usual morning or afternoon call, when there's no ship and date

tools.name: excursions_for_sailing
tools.description: For one sailing (id from search_sailings), each port day: hours ashore, docked or tender, how many tours fit that day, and the top categories there, with a link to the day's excursions page. Figures across tours only; no single tour.

tools.name: excursion_activity
tools.description: One category of excursion at a port by its slug: how many tours, how many fit a usual morning or afternoon call, typical length and price per person, the review-weighted average rating, and what these tours involve, in our words. Also how many of that kind fit one call (as port_excursions picks it), with see_tours_url, our page listing them; no single tour. Take the slug from port_excursions' categories for that port (map the user's words, such as "snorkelling" or "kayaking", to one of them yourself). An unknown slug returns an error listing the port's categories.

category.description: A category slug from port_excursions' categories for this port, e.g. snorkeling or whale-watching. Once our own set is live the slugs are: beach-and-snorkel (Beach and snorkel), scuba (Scuba), glaciers-and-wildlife (Glaciers and wildlife), whale-watching (Whale watching), food-and-drink (Food and drink), history-and-sightseeing (History and sightseeing), adventure (Adventure), private-and-small-group (Private and small group), passes-and-self-guided (Passes and self-guided)

date.description: A call date to fit the tours to

ship_id.description: With date: fit the tours to this ship's call (id from find or get_sailing)

call_type.description: Fit the tours to a usual morning or afternoon call, when there's no ship and date

tools.name: find_deals
tools.description: The current cruise deals from one departure port (port id from find), as our deals page for that port shows them: our picks (each with why it was picked and the evidence, e.g. a price drop or below its usual price), every line's lowest total to sail, and how many sailings are on sale in the next 12 months. From Australia, New Zealand or the UK, local_lead is the cheapest complete all-in in the local currency: quote it first there. Totals are for the party stated in each price (usually two adults). Quote prices only from the returned rows; book_url is our booking link.

from_port.description: Departure port id (from find), e.g. un:USMIA

tools.name: get_line
tools.description: A cruise line by id (from find): passengers' score overall, by topic (food, service, cabins...) and by traveller type (couples, families...), its ships ranked by score, its daily gratuities and Wi-Fi (Starlink, plan prices, each with the line's own source), its price-drop rule (whether you can claim a lower price after booking, and how it's paid back) and final-payment schedule, from its own terms (price_drop.claimable null means we found no rule on the line's own pages, not that it refuses; earlier_rule gives a guarantee that covered earlier bookings only), and its lowest all-in price for two in the next 12 months. Quote prices only from the returned rows.

line_id.description: Cruise line id (from find with kind line), e.g. royal-caribbean

tools.name: rank_ships
tools.description: Ships (or lines) ranked by passengers' scores out of 5: overall, by topic (food, service, upkeep, cabins, entertainment, crowding) or by traveller type (couples, families, first-timers...), optionally within one line. Top 10, best first (worst: true for the lowest). Only ships with 100+ reviews are ranked. Give each score with its review count.

line.description: Only this line's ships (line id from find)

topic.description: Rank by one topic instead of overall

traveller.description: Rank by one traveller type's score instead of overall

tools.name: get_worth_it
tools.description: Compare a cruise line’s drink package or bundled fare with buying drinks individually. Returns available package terms, source links and break-even consumption by drink type. Include drinks_per_day for a personal comparison or sailing_id for sailing-specific rates when available.

line_id.description: Cruise line id (from find), e.g. royal-caribbean, carnival-cruise-line, msc-cruises

drinks_per_day.description: Drinks a day the person expects, for a personal verdict

tools.name: get_transfers
tools.description: How to get from the airport to a cruise port (and back): every way (train, bus, shuttle, cruise line coach, taxi, rideshare, private car) with its price for two adults one way in the local currency, time, how it works, and the Best for most, Cheapest and Fastest tags, each fare with its dated official source. Give a port id (from find) or an airport's IATA code. Quote fares only as returned (an estimate stays an estimate, a part-of-the-way fare says so). The private car has a fare only where its seller publishes one for the trip; otherwise its fare is fixed when booked through book_url. Give the disclosure line with that link.

port_id.description: Cruise port id (from find), e.g. un:USMIA

tools.name: watch_sailing
tools.description: Start a price alert for the signed-in user on one sailing (id from search_sailings or get_sailing), for a party and cabin: we email them when the all-in price drops by 3% and at least $25, or below target_total_usd if given. Offer it after showing a sailing the user likes ("Want me to watch this price?"); call it only when they say yes. Needs the user's Cruise Register account: if they aren't connected yet, the result asks them to connect. Never tell the user a watch is set unless this call succeeded.

party.description: Who travels: 2A two adults (default), 1A one adult, 2A2C two adults and two children

cabin.description: Cabin class; any = the cheapest cabin

target_total_usd.description: Alert when the all-in total for the party falls to this, if the user names a price

tools.name: my_watches
tools.description: The signed-in user's price watches: each sailing, party and cabin, the price when they started watching and the latest price we checked. Needs the user's Cruise Register account.

tools.name: stop_watching
tools.description: Stop one of the signed-in user's price watches (watch_id from my_watches). Only when the user asks to stop it.
